summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted after developing hypotension, chest tightness, and a retro-orbital headache following hemodialysis. She presented with altered mental status that resolved with IV fluids. Workup revealed no evidence of acute stroke or myocardial infarction, with normal cardiac enzymes and a non-contrast head CT showing only chronic changes. Her hypotension was attributed to hypovolemia from dialysis and use of nitroglycerin, exacerbated by antihypertensive medications. The INR was elevated at 3.7, prompting temporary discontinuation of warfarin. She underwent a short session of ultrafiltration to optimize fluid balance. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with home health services, with instructions to resume adjusted medications, continue dialysis, monitor daily weight, adhere to a low-sodium diet, and follow up for INR monitoring.
